messages:
maria: Quick sync on telemetry we need for the soft-eviction / credit-fallback flow. I prototyped a histogram of eviction latencies but we need a concrete list of signals before I wire dashboards.

alex: Nice. Do we mean soft-eviction as in 'mark tenant soft-shed and route to lower-tier' + credits fallback?

maria: Yep. The flow: admission detects overload -> mark soft-shed -> attempt borrow from tenant credit pool -> if credit insufficient, route to fallback model variant / degraded path.

kyra: For SLOs we need two main observability surfaces: 1) decision events (why was a request soft-shed/evicted/borrowed), 2) resource impact (latency/cost change and success/error for that request).

sam: Agreed. Also we should capture causal tags on the request so downstream pipelines can attribute quality/regressions. Maybe attach header: x-redwood-admit-reason and x-redwood-credit-source.

jen: Security/abuse angle: we must record abuse-score snapshot at decision time (hash it), but avoid storing PII. Also flag repeated evictions per tenant as priority signal.

maria: Proposed minimal event schema (line-delimited JSON in events stream):
- event_type: admit_decision
- tenant_id (hashed)
- timestamp
- admit_result: [accepted|soft_shed|evicted|degraded]
- reason_code: [overload|abuse|quota_exhausted|policy]
- credit_change: {borrowed: n_tokens, remaining_pool: n_tokens}  <-- numeric fields OK
- fallback_variant: name|null
- latency_ms: total end-to-end
- sample_output_hash: short sha to link to evals

alex: We should keep it compact. Maybe collapse credit_change into two ints: borrowed_tokens and pool_after. Also avoid freeform maps — make the schema fixed.

maria: Good call. I'll make it fields borrowed_tokens and remaining_pool.

kyra: Instrumentation placement: admission service must emit admit_decision event synchronously (best-effort) and tracer annotations for request span. If event emission fails, still proceed with decision but increment a metric indicating lost-events.

sam: For rate limiting / quota boundaries we also need a sampling of raw tokens + sample of full request payload for debugging (with customer opt-in). We should never sample by default.

jen: Add an abuse_fingerprint field and abuse_score (0-100) at decision time. That lets us correlate evictions with abuse detection models without exposing model inputs.

maria: Thoughts on cardinality: tenant_id hashed plus route_id and model_variant. We need low-cardinality labels for high-cardinality telemetry and separate low-volume event stream with higher-cardinality blobs.

alex: Right. Metrics: counters and histograms (per-tenant aggregated): admit_counts{result}, borrowed_tokens_sum, eviction_rate, fallback_rate, decision_latency_histogram. Events: admit_decision stream with the schema above.

kyra: For dashboards, we want per-tenant SLA health: eviction_rate, borrow_rate, fallback_latency_penalty. Also an abuse-investigation view: recent admit_decisions for tenants with eviction spikes.

maria: Tradeoffs: emitting every decision with full schema increases event QPS significantly. Proposal: 100% counters/histograms plus 1% admit_decision sampling with deterministic reservoir for tenants over threshold (so we get more from hot tenants).

sam: Deterministic reservoir is good: hash(tenant_id) modulo X to bias sample. Also increase sampling to 5% when eviction_rate > threshold.

jen: For privacy/legal: ensure hashed tenant id salts are rotated per-month and access controls on raw events. Also redact any sampled payloads unless explicit customer consent.

maria: Operational playbook suggestions:
- Alert: tenant eviction_rate spikes > 2% sustained for 10m -> pager to oncall (SRE).
- Alert: borrow_pool_depletion -> runbook to check tenant quota usage and suspicious traffic.
- Dashboard: show recent admit_decision samples and linked traces.

alex: Interface boundary question: who owns the admit_decision schema? Admission service or telemetry infra?

maria: I think admission defines the schema and emits events; telemetry infra owns the ingestion contract, retention, and downstream dashboards. We'll version the schema with admit_v1, admit_v2.

kyra: Also define a light-weight admission API for Dedicated/Private deployments so they can emit the same events locally (or send to our remote collector if allowed). We should avoid coupling to internal Kafka topics.

sam: Implementation note: emit a minimal JSON over OTLP logs and attach attributes to spans. That makes it easy to route to either ES/kafka or our metrics pipeline.

jen: Abuse signals: we should increment a per-tenant abuse_score_rolling metric that admission can read back to make decisions, rather than always calling a heavy classifier synchronously. Keeps admission fast.

maria: Action items:
- maria: draft admit_v1 schema PR (events + metric names) -> due EOD Wed
- alex: sketch sampling & reservoir algorithm and cost estimate -> due Thu
- kyra: propose alert thresholds and dashboard mockups -> due Thu
- sam: prototype OTLP emission (small PR) -> due Fri
- jen: write privacy checklist for sampled payloads and hashed id rotation -> due Mon

healthbot: Reminder created: "admit_v1 schema PR" assigned to maria, due 1712540000.

maria: Thanks — I'll start the PR and ping folks. Any objections to the sampling defaults? 1% baseline, 5% hot-tenant, auto-increase when eviction_rate>2%?

alex: Sounds reasonable. We may tweak after cost numbers. +1

kyra: +1 from me. Let's also include a flag to force 100% sampling for an incident trace.

jen: +1. Add retention policy: sampled admit_decisions 30d, hot-tenant samples 90d, aggregated metrics forever.

maria: Great. I'll include retention and schema versioning in the PR. Closing thread for now, will update when PR is up. :thumbsup:
